headline: NDA Exam Eligibility 2026: Age, Qualification and Rules
metaDescription: NDA exam eligibility 2026: age 16.5 to 19.5 years, Class 12 pass required, PCM compulsory for Air Force and Navy wings, unmarried candidates, no attempt limit.

sections.content:
The National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination, conducted by the Union Public Service Commission, is the main gateway for school leavers to become officers in the Indian Armed Forces. It is held twice a year as NDA 1 and NDA 2, and successful candidates train at the National Defence Academy in Khadakwasla before moving to their service academies. The NDA 2 2026 notification declared 394 vacancies across the Army, Navy, Air Force and Naval Academy entry scheme.

Eligibility rests on four pillars: nationality, age, education and marital status. Candidates must be Indian citizens, between 16.5 and 19.5 years old, have passed or be appearing in Class 12, and be unmarried. There is no age relaxation for any category, which makes the NDA one of the strictest entry schemes in India. Missing the age window by even a day means waiting for no later chance.
sections.title: What the NDA Exam Is and Who Can Apply

sections.content:
The age rule is precise: candidates must be between 16.5 and 19.5 years at the course commencement date, with exact birth-date ranges in each notification. For NDA 2 2026, candidates born between 2 January 2008 and 1 July 2011 were eligible. Unlike most government exams, there is no relaxation for SC, ST, OBC or any other category, and the same limit applies to male and female candidates.

On education, the Army wing accepts a Class 12 pass in any stream, while the Air Force and Naval wings require Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in the 10+2 pattern. Students appearing in their Class 12 finals can apply provisionally, but must produce proof of passing before joining. Only unmarried candidates may apply, and they must remain unmarried until training is complete.
sections.title: Age, Education and Marital Rules in Detail

sections.content:
The written examination has two papers: Mathematics for 300 marks and the General Ability Test for 600 marks, covering English, general knowledge, physics, chemistry, geography, history and current affairs. Candidates who clear the written cutoff are called for the Services Selection Board interview, a five-day process testing personality, leadership, group skills and psychological fitness through interviews, group tasks and psychological tests.

The SSB carries 900 marks, equal to the written exam, so personality and leadership matter as much as academics. Candidates recommended by the SSB undergo medical examination against strict service standards, including vision and physical fitness norms that vary by wing. Air Force flying branch candidates face the most demanding medical and pilot aptitude tests.
sections.title: Exam Pattern and the SSB Interview

sections.content:
Final merit is drawn from combined written and SSB marks, and selected candidates join the National Defence Academy for three years of joint training alongside cadets from all three services. Army cadets then move to the Indian Military Academy, naval cadets to the Indian Naval Academy, and air force cadets to the Air Force Academy for a further year of specialized training before commissioning as officers.

Preparation should start early: Class 11 and 12 mathematics and science form the backbone of the written exam, while regular reading of current affairs builds the General Ability Test score. For the SSB, group discussions, outdoor activities and honest self-assessment help far more than coaching alone. Candidates should also track the official UPSC notification each cycle, since birth-date windows and vacancy numbers change every exam.
